Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the PrecisionMed Devices Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO; Mike Thompson, CFO; Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. PrecisionMed Devices delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance:
1. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
2. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
3. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
4. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
5. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives

Mike will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with overall performance highlights and key achievements. We're thrilled with the outstanding quarter, which underscores the strength of our portfolio and the execution of our Innovation-First strategy amid a dynamic medtech landscape.

On the topline, we delivered Q2 revenue of $2.75 billion, representing 12% reported growth and 14% organic growth year-over-year. This handily beat our guidance midpoint and consensus expectations by $75 million. For the full year, we're now raising our organic growth outlook to 10-13%, up from 9-12%, reflecting robust procedural volumes, share gains, and accelerating adoption of our premium technologies. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.68, a 15% increase, driven by 320 basis points of operating margin expansion to 28.5%. Gross margins expanded 210 basis points to 66.2%, fueled by favorable mix shift toward high-margin Structural Heart and Electrophysiology products, pricing discipline, and supply chain efficiencies following resolutions to our 2023 resin shortages.

Let me break this down by our core franchises, where we saw broad-based strength. Cardiovascular, our largest segment at 48% of revenue, grew 16% organically to $1.32 billion. Structural Heart was the star, up 22%, propelled by the global rollout of our Evolut FX TAVR platform, which captured 28% U.S. market share in low-risk patients—gaining 400 basis points on competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien series. We performed over 45,000 TAVR procedures worldwide in the quarter, a 19% increase, benefiting from aging demographics and expanded Medicare reimbursement for younger patients. Electrophysiology surged 25% to $420 million, with our Affera Mapping System—now with integrated AI for real-time lesion prediction—securing CE Mark in Europe and driving 35% procedure growth in AFib ablations.

Neuromodulation and Pain Management, 22% of revenue, posted 11% organic growth to $605 million. Key here was the U.S. launch of our Intellis II SCS system with next-gen BurstDR stimulation, which achieved 42% same-store growth in implant volumes at top IDNs like Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic partners. We're seeing a shift from traditional tonic stimulation, with our adaptive closed-loop tech reducing opioid dependency in chronic pain patients by up to 60% in clinical data.

Surgical Innovations, up 9% to $510 million, benefited from our Hugo RAS robotic-assisted surgery platform, which completed its first 500 U.S. cases post-FDA clearance in March. This positions us to challenge Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci dominance, with cost-per-procedure 20% lower and superior ergonomics for complex gyn and urologic cases.

Diagnostics and Monitoring, our growth engine at 18% organic expansion to $495 million, rode the wave of our Reveal LINQ+ ICM with AI anomaly detection, which saw 30% adoption in Europe following NHS framework inclusion. Partnerships with Philips for integrated remote monitoring are scaling to 2 million patients by year-end.

Regionally, performance was equally impressive. The U.S., 55% of revenue, grew 13% organically, outpacing the 7% market per LEK Consulting procedural data, thanks to our 1,200+ field clinical specialists driving utilization. Share in TAVR and EP now at 27% and 32%, respectively. Europe, 25%, accelerated to 15% growth, with double-digit gains in Germany and the UK amid streamlined DRG reimbursements for our TAVR and neuromod systems. We're navigating pricing pressures from HTA reviews but offsetting with volume from 25 new hospital contracts. Asia-Pacific, 15%, exploded 22% organically, led by China where our J-Vent TAVR received NMPA approval in Q1, generating $85 million in initial ramp—faster than Abbott's early days there. Japan and India contributed via endoscopy expansions, tapping into a $15 billion TAM growing at 12% CAGR per Grand View Research. Emerging markets rounded out at 5%, up 18%, with strong traction in Brazil for our affordable pacing leads.

Key achievements this quarter solidify our leadership. Regulatory milestones include FDA approval for the Percept PC Neurostimulator with BrainSense tech, enabling biomarker-based adaptive DBS for Parkinson's—first-to-market capability that could add $300 million in peak sales. We also expanded indications for our Aquablation therapy in BPH, now covering prostates up to 250cc. On technical initiatives, we invested $285 million in R&D, 11% of revenue, advancing our Digital Ecosystem platform—an AWS-integrated cloud solution aggregating device data for predictive analytics. Early pilots with 50 U.S. health systems reduced readmissions by 25% in heart failure cohorts, positioning us for value-based care contracts akin to Medtronic's CareLink evolution. Strategically, we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of NeuroPace in late Q1, instantly doubling our responsive neurostim for epilepsy market share to 45%. We announced a $500 million manufacturing expansion in Galway, Ireland, for resilience against geopolitical risks, targeting 98% on-time delivery by FY25. Sustainability-wise, 65% of our devices now incorporate recycled materials, aligning with EU MDR and scoring us top ESG ratings from MSCI.

Looking at trends, we're capitalizing on macro tailwinds: a 5 million annual increase in global 65+ populations driving device demand; the shift to ambulatory surgery centers, where our portfolio penetration hit 35%; and AI/ML integration, with our algorithms now boasting 95% accuracy in arrhythmia detection per recent NEJM Catalyst study. Challenges like inflation and talent shortages were mitigated via 8% cost savings from robotic automation in assembly lines. Strategically, our insights point to three pillars: Premium Innovation, 75% of pipeline; Procedural Enablement, doubling clinical rep headcount to 2,500; and Global Scale, aiming for 30% APAC revenue by 2027. We're confident in sustaining 8-10% CAGR through the decade, outpacing the 6% industry average per Evaluate MedTech.

Now, let's talk about our strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter. These build directly on the momentum from our Q2 results, where we delivered 14% year-over-year revenue growth to $2.75 billion, driven by a 22% surge in our structural heart franchise and resilient margins at 28.5% adjusted gross margin.

Our priorities are laser-focused on three pillars: accelerating innovation in high-growth segments, expanding global market access amid favorable reimbursement tailwinds, and enhancing operational resilience to navigate macroeconomic headwinds like inflation and supply chain disruptions. We're allocating $300 million—or about 11% of projected Q3 revenue—to R&D, underscoring our commitment to outpacing the industry's 12-15% CAGR in minimally invasive procedures through FY2027, per Grand View Research data.

First, we'll prioritize the full commercial ramp of next-gen platforms, targeting 25% of Q3 revenue mix. The full U.S. commercial launch of our Evolut FX TAVR system follows 35% procedure growth in Q2 limited release, capturing share in moderate- and high-risk patients. With 95% hemodynamic stability at 30 days, it addresses the $8 billion U.S. TAVR market expanding at 15% annually due to aging demographics—Baby Boomers now 45% of procedures. We'll deploy 150 clinical specialists across top IDNs like Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic, aiming for 5,500 implants in Q3 versus 4,500 in Q2, contributing $350 million in revenue at a 65% attach rate for ancillary imaging consumables.

Internationally, we'll accelerate CE Mark expansion into Japan and China, partnering with Terumo for localized distribution. Japan’s TAVR market, valued at ¥150 billion, is underserved with only 18,000 annual procedures despite 28% prevalence of severe aortic stenosis in those over 80—we project 20% share capture by year-end through our J-TEVAR variant.

Second, we're doubling down on digital health and AI integration to drive 10-12% productivity gains. Our AI-enabled PrecisionNav platform for robotic-assisted surgery, integrating generative AI for real-time procedural guidance akin to enhancements in Hugo RAS, saw Q2 pilots in 25 U.S. centers yield 18% reduction in operative times and 22% lower complication rates for complex mitral valve repairs, unlocking a $4.5 billion RAS market growing at 16% CAGR.

In Q3, we'll roll out Version 2.0 with predictive analytics for tissue characterization, targeting 40% adoption in our 500 installed base. This includes investment in cloud-based interoperability with EHR systems like Epic and Cerner, compliant with HL7 FHIR standards. We expect this to boost recurring revenue from service contracts to 35% of segment sales, up from 28%, while improving hospital ROI to under 18 months—critical as capex budgets tighten amid 4-6% Medicare reimbursement cuts. Regionally, EMEA will see 25% of Q3 RAS installs in Germany and the UK, leveraging EU MDR tailwinds and NHS frameworks. APAC exposure ramps to 18% via our Singapore hub, focusing on India's private hospital network where RAS penetration is just 5% versus 25% in the U.S.

Third, we'll deepen penetration in high-growth emerging markets, where structural heart devices expand at 22% CAGR per IQVIA data. Our CardioShield left atrial appendage closure device achieved 92% implant success in Q2 China trials. In Q3, we'll launch in Brazil and India post-ANVISA and CDSCO approvals, targeting 3,000 procedures at $8,500 ASP, driving $25 million incremental revenue.

U.S. remains core at 55% of revenue, but we're shifting mix: EMEA to 26% via bundled CRM-ICD offerings with our Assert subcutaneous ICD, and APAC to 16% amid China's 14th Five-Year Plan prioritizing medtech localization. Reimbursement wins include CMS pass-through status for CardioShield, adding 150 basis points to blended ASPs.

Operationally, we're fortifying supply chains against resin inflation up 8% YoY and Taiwan semiconductor risks by qualifying new suppliers in Mexico and Vietnam, reducing China dependency from 35% to 22%. This supports Q3 gross margin guidance of 29-30%, with OpCo efficiencies targeting 250 bps expansion through LEAN Six Sigma in our Galway facility—our largest structural heart hub. M&A scouting remains active, tracking tuck-ins for electrophysiology ablation catheters with 20%+ synergies.

In summary, these priorities position us to deliver Q3 revenue of $2.85-2.95 billion, 11-14% growth, with EPS of $1.85-1.95.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. As we wrap up a strong Q2, our R&D investment and robust pipeline progress form a cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy in the $500 billion-plus global medical devices market. We're committed to pushing boundaries in minimally invasive therapies, digital integration, and precision medicine, especially in structural heart, neuromodulation, and robotics-assisted innovations.

In Q2, we invested $285 million in R&D, representing 11% of revenue—up from prior periods and above the industry average of 10-12%, as reported by Evaluate MedTech. Peers like Medtronic and Boston Scientific are at 11-13%, but we're investing aggressively to fuel a pipeline of 28 programs, with 12 in late-stage development. This is yielding returns: our R&D efficiency ratio—pipeline value added per dollar spent—improved to 4.2x from 3.8x a year ago, driven by milestones and partnerships.

By focus area, 45% or $128 million went to structural heart and cardiovascular, addressing aging populations and rising AFib. 30% or $85 million supported neuromodulation and neurovascular, capitalizing on chronic pain and stroke surges. The remaining 25% fueled robotics and digital health, including AI/ML for predictive analytics.

Pipeline progress hit 85% of key milestones on time, thanks to our agile model. In structural heart, our next-generation Evolut FX TAVR system, with 20% lower profile than leaders like Edwards' Sapien 3 Ultra, completed pivotal IDE trial enrollment ahead of schedule. With 450 patients across 35 U.S. sites, interim data showed 95% procedural success and 2.1% 30-day mortality, competitive with TVT Registry evidence. We're on track for FDA IDE supplement in Q4 2024 and PMA by mid-2025, eyeing a $4-5 billion market at 15% CAGR.

In neuromodulation, our Intellis II SCS with directional burst stimulation and adaptive AI received CE Mark six months post-submission. Early European data from 200 implants shows 65% pain reduction at 6 months, beating SENZA benchmarks. U.S. pivotal trial is 75% enrolled, topline Q1 2025. Europe's MDR pathway gives a head start, boosting German and UK channels where neuromod grew 22% YoY.

Robotics shines with Hugo RAS third-gen, achieving first-in-human in Asia under Japan PMDA breakthrough. Sub-millimeter accuracy and 4D CT reduce soft-tissue damage 30%. We're investing $25 million in APAC studies for NMPA China by late 2024. APAC is 25% of pipeline opportunity, robotics at 18% CAGR per Grand View.

We're embedding digital twins and generative AI to cut preclinical timelines 25%, like HeartSync ML for valve durability. Sustainability: 40% new materials bioresorbable, aligning with EU Green Deal and CMS Bundled Payments.

Ahead, Q3 R&D at $300 million supports five catalysts: FDA approvals, trial readouts, Asia launch. This drives 15-18% EPS growth in 2025, pipeline NPV over $8 billion. Capital allocation: 90% organic, 10% tuck-ins like wearables.

Next, organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Excluding our NeuroPace acquisition and 150 bps FX headwinds, we achieved robust 14% organic growth, accelerating from prior quarters and our strongest since pre-pandemic. This stemmed from procedural recovery, premium mix ASP dynamics, and pipeline ramps.

By segments, broad strength prevailed. Cardiovascular, 48% of revenue, grew 16% organically to $1.32 billion. Volumes surged on structural heart and coronary, with Evolut FX—over 45,000 implants—driving mid-teens growth via PROPEL-like data outperforming Sapien. EP's Affera AI mapping added 25%, on ablation rebounds.

Neuromodulation and Pain, 22%, hit 11% to $605 million. Intellis II BurstDR gained in opioid-sparing back pain, shifting from tonic stim.

Surgical Innovations, 9% to $510 million. Hugo RAS 500 cases post-clearance, lower costs vs da Vinci.

Diagnostics, 18% to $495 million. Reveal LINQ+ AI and Philips partnerships scaling monitoring.

Geographically, U.S. 55%, 13% organic to ~$1.51B, beating market via IDN specialists, 98% 2019 procedure levels, 2% share gain per IQVIA.

Europe 25%, 15% to ~$688M, strong Germany/UK on TAVR/robotics, NICE guidelines.

Asia-Pacific 15%, 22% to ~$413M, China TAVR $85M ramp, Japan/India endoscopy.

Emerging 5%, 18%, Brazil pacing.

This underscores our Innovate to Penetrate strategy: 12% R&D yielded launches driving 3 points growth, 120 bps share gain YTD, MedTech Cloud boosting adherence 18%. Supply resilience: 95% onshoring.

Q3 organic 12-14%, FY24 raised to 10-13%. Tailwinds: demographics, outpatient shift $150B TAM per McKinsey; risks: reimbursement, China pricing.

Finally, impact of pricing and cost management initiatives. Facing reimbursement pressures, EU MDR, CMS IPPS FY2025 cuts, we've offset via execution for margin gains and cash acceleration.

Pricing achieved 4.2% YoY core ASP increase, third straight quarter up from 3.1% Q1. Value-based pricing: Structural Heart outcome contracts with IDNs linked to readmissions drove 6.8% TAVR uplift, $45M top-line.

Mix optimization: 12% shift to high-margin Surgical/Robotics like Hugo Xi+, 25-30% premiums, adding 150 bps gross margins. U.S. 55%, navigated 2.7% CMS ortho cut, passing 70% via contracts, flat ASPs hips/knees, share vs Stryker/Zimmer.

EMEA 25%, MDR $18M costs offset by 5.1% increases on AI imaging. Emerging 20%, 2.5% ASP despite China NRDL, via neuromod bundles.

Costs: $62M annualized savings, 15% beat. Gross margins +220 bps to 68.4%, highest in five years. Supply: 35% localized Mexico/Vietnam, 18% logistics cut post-Red Sea.

Manufacturing: digital twins/Industry 4.0 in Galway/Plymouth cut pacemaker cycles 22%, $28M savings. AI forecasting hedged resin/titanium 70% below spot.

R&D rationalized: pruned projects, realloc $40M to scaffolds, R&D % to 11%. SG&A: zero-based trimmed 8% travel/consulting, offset sales robotics.

Positions for 300+ bps annual gross expansion to 2026, bundled BPCI, Asia co-dev with Mindray. Q3 pricing 4%+, savings $75M. Buffered 3% FX, raised FY24: growth 10-13%, EPS $6.85-$6.95.

I will now turn the call over to Mike for a review of our financial results.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. Revenue reached $2.75 billion, up 12% as reported and 14% organically, beating expectations. Gross profit was $1.82 billion, with margins at 66.2%, benefiting from mix, pricing, and efficiencies. Operating expenses were controlled, with R&D at $285 million or 11% of revenue, SG&A at 25%, leading to adjusted operating income of $784 million, margins 28.5%. Adjusted EPS $1.68, up 15%. Cash from operations was robust at $850 million, supporting $200 million in dividends, $300 million share repurchases, and debt reduction. Balance sheet solid, net debt to EBITDA 2.1x.

For FY2024, we're raising organic revenue growth to 10-13%, adjusted EPS to $6.85-$6.95, implying 14% growth. Q3 revenue $2.85-2.95 billion, EPS $1.85-1.95. Margins to expand further on efficiencies.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lena for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Lena Patel:
Thank you, Mike. I'm excited to share updates on our innovative pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for the Percept PC Neurostimulator with BrainSense, enabling adaptive DBS for Parkinson's via biomarkers—first-to-market, potential $300M peak. Also, expanded Aquablation for larger prostates.

Pipeline advances include Evolut FX TAVR IDE progress, Intellis II SCS CE Mark and U.S. trial momentum, Hugo RAS Asia firsts. Digital Ecosystem pilots reducing readmissions 25%. Seven late-stage programs position us for launches driving growth.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Lena. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, congrats on the quarter. Alex, can you elaborate on TAVR share gains and sustainability against Edwards and Abbott?

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. Our Evolut FX captured 28% U.S. low-risk share, up 400 bps, via superior hemodynamics and 45,000 global procedures, 19% up. Aging demographics, Medicare expansions help. With specialists and data from pilots, we expect continued gains, targeting 30%+ share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. Mike, on the impressive margin expansion to 66.2% gross, how sustainable with pricing pressures and costs?

Mike Thompson:
Lisa, thanks. Expansion from mix to premium Structural Heart/EP, 210 bps gross via efficiencies post-resin issues, pricing discipline 4.2% ASP. Costs $62M savings annualized, localization, automation. Q3 29-30% gross, 300 bps annual through 2026 on continued initiatives.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you for that insight, Mike.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Davis with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Davis:
Thanks. Tom, on APAC explosion to 22% growth, details on China ramp and emerging priorities?

Tom Hargrove:
Mark, China J-Vent TAVR $85M post-NMPA, faster than peers, plus Japan/India endoscopy. Q3 priorities: LAAC launches Brazil/India 3,000 procedures, APAC mix to 16%, Terumo partnerships, localization per 14th Plan. 22% CAGR tailwinds strong.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Appreciate it, Tom.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez:
Thanks. Lena, on R&D pipeline, timelines for key catalysts and any regulatory risks?

Dr. Lena Patel:
Emily, 85% milestones on time. Evolut FX PMA mid-2025, Intellis II U.S. topline Q1 2025, Hugo NMPA late 2024. Risks mitigated by agile model, digital twins cutting timelines 25%, partnerships. Five Q3/Q4 catalysts: approvals, readouts.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
